intro.h2: A father-and-son company with its own crew
paragraphs: Rohrer For Construction has offered kitchen and bath remodeling in Lake County, IL since 1989. Adolph Rohrer founded the company, and today he and his son Austin run it together. Most of the work is done by their own crew, a team that has worked together for more than 35 years, which keeps quality and communication in one place.

Kitchens and baths lead the list, but the same crew also finishes basements, builds additions, garages and decks, and handles exteriors. That range helps when a bathroom job uncovers framing or plumbing that needs attention. Permits in towns like Grayslake, Libertyville and Mundelein are handled for you.

services.h2: Kitchen and bath remodeling in Lake County, IL, and beyond

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Full renovations, layout fixes, small-kitchen makeovers and open-concept updates, planned around cabinet storage, prep space and traffic flow. A moderate Lake County kitchen typically runs $25,000 to $75,000; custom cabinetry and high-end finishes can run higher.

image.alt: Kitchen remodel with gray Shaker cabinets, white quartz counters, stainless appliances and oak floors

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Guest baths to primary suites, built with Schluter waterproofing and fixtures from brands like Delta and Kohler. A typical bathroom takes 2 to 4 weeks, depending on whether it needs new tile, a plumbing move or a full gut renovation.

image.alt: Gurnee bathroom remodel with a deep green Shaker vanity, white top and light porcelain floor

items.name: Showers and Tub Conversions
items.blurb: Walk-in, curbless and enclosed showers, tub-to-shower conversions and bathtub replacements. For a curbless shower the crew first checks floor depth and the drain route, then builds slope, waterproofing, tile and glass as one project, with blocking for grab bars where needed.

image.alt: Shower with dark-framed sliding glass door, gray wood-look wall tile and a low white shower base

items.name: Basement Finishing
items.blurb: Unfinished lower levels turned into usable rooms, from open family spaces with new flooring and lighting to specialty features like a basement sauna. Framing, insulation, drywall and flooring are handled by the same crew that does your kitchen.

image.alt: Finished basement with black painted open ceiling, recessed lights, black doors and light wood-look vinyl floor

items.name: Additions, Garages and Outdoor Living
items.blurb: Room additions, second-floor additions, garages, decks, pergolas and screen houses. Planning, permits, construction and the final walkthrough are managed by the same team, so even a larger, multi-phase project still has one point of contact from start to finish.

image.alt: Screen house addition with white siding, gable windows and patio seating on a paver pad

why_choose_us.h2: Why Lake County homeowners stick with Rohrer

items.title: Owners on the job
items.text: Adolph manages the jobsite as President, and Austin leads client relations as Vice President, so you deal with an owner from the first planning call to the final walkthrough.

items.title: Mostly in-house work
items.text: Unlike companies that subcontract everything, Rohrer's own experienced crew does the majority of the work, which means tighter quality control and fewer hand-offs.

items.title: Credentials you can check
items.text: Licensed, insured and bonded, BBB Accredited with an A+ rating, and rated 5.0 from 20 Google reviews. Reviewers call the crew consistent, communicative, punctual and very detail oriented.

items.title: Financing through RenoFi
items.text: A referral partnership with RenoFi gives homeowners access to loans built for renovations, which the company says often carry better rates. The process is simple and carries no obligation.

about.text: Adolph Rohrer founded Rohrer For Construction in 1989 to give Lake County homeowners honest, high-quality remodeling. As President, he runs jobsite management and brings decades of hands-on construction experience to how each project is planned and built. His son Austin Rohrer is Vice President of client relations. He leads planning talks and helps homeowners turn rough ideas into a clear scope. Together they have grown the business into a full-service remodeler, and they host a Facebook group where homeowners can ask remodeling questions.

image.alt: Adolph Rohrer, founder and President of Rohrer For Construction

process.h2: From first walkthrough to final review

steps.title: Free in-person quote
steps.text: The team walks through your project on site, hears your goals and layout frustrations, and gives an accurate, no-pressure quote.

steps.title: Scope and planning
steps.text: Layout, cabinet planning, finish selections, budget and permits are organized before construction begins, so everyone works from the same plan.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: The in-house crew builds with a focus on craftsmanship, detail and regular updates, while permits and inspections are handled along the way.

steps.title: Final walkthrough
steps.text: You review the finished room together to confirm it matches the original plan and your expectations before the job is closed out.

service_area.text: Rohrer works within roughly 20 miles of Lindenhurst. That covers northern and central Lake County, from Antioch and Fox Lake down to Libertyville and Mundelein, and south toward Buffalo Grove and Lake Forest. Across the state line, the crew also supports Kenosha, Pleasant Prairie, Salem, Bristol and Twin Lakes. Projects just outside the radius may still qualify, so reach out anyway.

items.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Lake County?
items.a: A moderate kitchen renovation typically runs $25,000 to $75,000, depending on size, materials and scope. Projects with custom cabinetry and high-end finishes can run higher, and moving plumbing or appliances adds work. Rohrer gives free, detailed estimates so you know what to expect before anything starts.

items.q: How long does a bathroom remodel take?
items.a: In Rohrer's experience a typical bathroom takes 2 to 4 weeks. New tile, a relocated drain or a full gut each change the schedule. You get a clear timeline at the start and regular updates while the crew works, so you know when the room will be ready to use again.

items.q: Do I need a permit for my remodel?
items.a: Most structural, electrical and plumbing work and all additions need permits in Lake County towns such as Grayslake, Libertyville and Mundelein. Rohrer handles the permit process for you and builds to local code, with the goal of passing inspection the first time.

items.q: Do you do more than kitchens and baths?
items.a: Yes. The same crew finishes basements, builds room additions, garages and decks, and handles exterior painting and siding. Specialty jobs like a basement sauna, screen houses and pergolas are in the portfolio too. One contractor for a mixed project means fewer hand-offs and clearer accountability.

Yes. Rohrer has a referral partnership with RenoFi, a lender focused on renovation loans that, according to the company, often offers better rates than traditional options. The process is simple and carries no obligation, so you can check your numbers while you plan the project.

final_cta.text: Call (847) 668-7183 for a free in-person quote, or post a question in the Rohrer Facebook group if you are still deciding.
